correctness.rationale: The equality of the two-column plus/minus norm sum forces disjoint support: Jensen at exponent p/2 followed by strict subadditivity (p<2) or superadditivity (p>2) gives a fixed strict sign for each row with two nonzero entries. This includes p=1, and the converse follows by summing over disjoint supports. With n−1 nonempty supports in n rows there is either one blank row or exactly one doubled column. A doubled column with fixed signs has the interval parameter t=|b|^p; its endpoints are precisely the two singleton placements. The intervals and vertices form a compact graph mapped continuously and bijectively onto the Hausdorff embedding space. Counting the signed row placements gives V=2^(n−1)n!, and moving any one column into the blank row with either sign gives degree 2(n−1), hence the stated E. The unsigned moves generate all permutations; an out-and-back move flips any one column sign. Collapsing the spanning tree gives a homotopy-equivalent quotient wedge of E−V+1 circles; the source's wording 'deformation-retracts onto' need not hold as a literal subspace assertion. Its stated homotopy and homology conclusions hold. The entrywise signed power p/q preserves the supports and maps p-unit columns to q-unit columns with a continuous inverse. The n=2 graph is a four-cycle. A fresh bounded enumeration found (V,E,beta_1)=(4,4,1),(24,48,25),(192,576,385),(1920,7680,5761),(23040,115200,92161), each connected and of the stated degree. It checks finite incidence only, not the all-dimensional homeomorphism.
residual_risks: The support argument does not apply at p=2; complex, p=infinity, and higher codimension are outside this assessment.
